extracted.intended_audience: journalists, newsroom editors, and general news readers
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and expectations about plagiarism and corrections in journalism, as illustrated by a news report about a reporter who copied other outlets' reporting. Focuses on what counts as misconduct, newsroom remedies, and disciplinary consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism is a 'cardinal sin in journalism'
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is one of the cardinal sins in journalism."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit statement of the severity of plagiarism in the profession; frames copying another outlet's work as fundamentally unethical and inexcusable. Article repeats the reporter's own apology language: "It was wrong. It was inexcusable."

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not present another newspaper's work as your own
rubrics_metrics.description: "I used another newspaper's work as if it were my own."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The core prohibition: using reporting produced by another outlet without attribution or passing it off as original reporting. The article gives the reporter's confession as the exemplar of this breach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid copying substantial portions of others' stories
rubrics_metrics.description: The Post says the reporter "lifted two paragraphs from one Republic story and 10 paragraphs from another."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amount and substance of copied text matter — lifting multiple paragraphs from other stories is presented as evidence of serious misconduct. Shows that 'substantial parts' can be measured in paragraph counts and treated as grounds for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: News organizations should publicly correct and apologize to affected outlets/readers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Post has "posted an 'editor's note' apologizing to the Republic and its readers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedial practice: publish an editor's note or correction that acknowledges the source harmed and apologizes. This is presented as the newsroom's appropriate response to discovered copying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional discipline (suspension) is an appropriate consequence
rubrics_metrics.description: Horwitz "has been suspended by the Post for three months."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example of internal disciplinary action taken by a newsroom for plagiarism; indicates that suspension (and presumably other formal sanctions) are considered appropriate responses to ethical breaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pressure (e.g., tight deadlines) is an explanation, not an excuse
rubrics_metrics.description: "Under the pressure of tight deadlines, I did something I have never done in my entire career."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article presents 'tight deadlines' as the reporter's explanation for the misconduct but, through the apology phrasing, treats it as not excusing the behavior — reinforcing that contextual pressures do not justify plagiarism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability to readers, colleagues, and the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: "To our readers, my friends and colleagues, my editors, and to the paper I love, I want to apologize."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes the obligation journalists have to multiple stakeholders (readers, colleagues, editors, and the institution) to maintain ethical standards and to make amends when they fail.
